questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML is the markup language used to structure web content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: HTML is the markup language used to structure web content.

questions.question: Which statement best describes HTML?
options: A markup language for structuring content
questions.explanation: HTML defines structure; CSS handles presentation and JavaScript adds behavior.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: HTML defines structure; CSS handles presentation and JavaScript adds behavior.

questions.question: Which declaration is used for a modern HTML document?
questions.explanation: The short doctype declaration tells the browser to use standards mode.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The short doctype declaration tells the browser to use standards mode.

questions.question: Which element contains the visible page content?
questions.explanation: The body contains the page's rendered content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The body contains the page's rendered content.

questions.question: Which element contains metadata and links to stylesheets?
questions.explanation: The head contains information about the document, such as title, metadata, and stylesheet links.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The head contains information about the document, such as title, metadata, and stylesheet links.

questions.question: What is an HTML element?
options: The opening tag, content, and closing tag where applicable
questions.explanation:
For example,

Hello

is a paragraph element.
questions.simpleExplanation:
Remember: For example,

Hello

is a paragraph element.

questions.question: Which element sets the document title shown in the browser tab?
questions.explanation: The title element belongs inside head and names the document.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The title element belongs inside head and names the document.

questions.question: Which attribute identifies the language of the document?
questions.explanation: For example, <html lang="en"> declares English as the page language.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: For example, <html lang="en"> declares English as the page language.

questions.question: Which is a correct minimal document structure?
questions.explanation: A standard document has doctype, html, head, and body in that order.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A standard document has doctype, html, head, and body in that order.

questions.question: What is the purpose of comments in HTML?
options: To add notes not rendered as page content
questions.explanation: HTML comments use <!-- comment --> and are not displayed as normal page content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: HTML comments use <!-- comment --> and are not displayed as normal page content.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to write an attribute value with spaces?
questions.explanation: Quotes safely group an attribute value that contains spaces.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Quotes safely group an attribute value that contains spaces.

questions.question: Which element represents the most important heading level?
questions.explanation: HTML provides heading levels h1 through h6.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: HTML provides heading levels h1 through h6.

questions.question: Which element is a void element?
questions.explanation: Void elements do not have closing tags; examples include br, img, input, and hr.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Void elements do not have closing tags; examples include br, img, input, and hr.

questions.question: Which entity displays a less-than sign as text?
questions.explanation: < represents < and > represents >.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: < represents < and > represents >.

questions.question: Which element is commonly used as a generic inline container?
questions.explanation: Span has no inherent semantic meaning and is commonly used inline.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Span has no inherent semantic meaning and is commonly used inline.

questions.question: Which element is a generic block-level container with no inherent semantic meaning?
questions.explanation: Div is a generic container; modern layout is usually controlled with CSS.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Div is a generic container; modern layout is usually controlled with CSS.

questions.question: What does the <hr> element traditionally represent?
options: A horizontal rule only, with no meaning
A thematic break between paragraph-level sections
questions.explanation: HR represents a thematic break; its appearance can be styled with CSS.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: HR represents a thematic break; its appearance can be styled with CSS.

questions.question: Which statement about HTML tag names is generally correct?
questions.explanation: HTML tag names are case-insensitive, and lowercase is the standard convention.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: HTML tag names are case-insensitive, and lowercase is the standard convention.

questions.question: What does the <em> element convey?
questions.explanation: Em conveys stress emphasis, often rendered in italics by default.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Em conveys stress emphasis, often rendered in italics by default.

questions.question: What is the semantic difference between <strong> and <b>?
options: Strong marks importance; b draws attention without adding the same importance meaning
B is semantic and strong is not
They are identical in every respect
questions.explanation: Their default appearance can be similar, but their meaning differs.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Their default appearance can be similar, but their meaning differs.

questions.question: Which attribute gives an anchor's destination?
questions.explanation: The href attribute specifies the linked URL or destination.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The href attribute specifies the linked URL or destination.

questions.question: Which is a relative URL?
questions.explanation: A relative URL is resolved from the current document or base URL.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A relative URL is resolved from the current document or base URL.

questions.question: Which scheme can open an email composition window?
questions.explanation: A mailto link can open the user's configured email app.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A mailto link can open the user's configured email app.

questions.question: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.explanation: Alt text communicates the image's relevant information when it cannot be seen.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Alt text communicates the image's relevant information when it cannot be seen.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the image file?
questions.explanation: Src points to the image resource.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Src points to the image resource.

questions.question: What is the purpose of loading='lazy' on an offscreen image?
options: Delays loading until it is near the viewport
questions.explanation: Lazy loading can reduce initial loading work for offscreen images.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Lazy loading can reduce initial loading work for offscreen images.

questions.question: Which elements are paired for a semantic figure and caption?
questions.explanation: Figure groups self-contained content and figcaption provides its caption.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Figure groups self-contained content and figcaption provides its caption.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <picture> element?
options: To offer alternate image sources with an img fallback
questions.explanation: Picture and source can support responsive images or different image formats.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Picture and source can support responsive images or different image formats.

questions.question: Which attribute opens a link in a new browsing context?
questions.explanation: Target blank requests a new tab or window depending on browser behavior.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Target blank requests a new tab or window depending on browser behavior.

questions.question: Which rel value is commonly used with target='_blank' to prevent opener access?
questions.explanation: Rel noopener prevents the opened page from accessing the opener window; noreferrer can also suppress referrer information.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Rel noopener prevents the opened page from accessing the opener window; noreferrer can also suppress referrer information.

questions.question: Which element creates an ordered list?
questions.explanation: Ol creates a list whose order is meaningful or numbered.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Ol creates a list whose order is meaningful or numbered.

questions.question: Which element creates an unordered list?
questions.explanation: Ul normally displays a bulleted list.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Ul normally displays a bulleted list.

questions.question: Which element represents an item in an ordered or unordered list?
questions.explanation: Li is a list item inside ul or ol.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Li is a list item inside ul or ol.

questions.question: In a description list, which element marks the term?
questions.explanation: Dt is the term; dd contains its description.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Dt is the term; dd contains its description.

questions.question: Which element creates a table row?
questions.explanation: Tr groups table cells into a row.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Tr groups table cells into a row.

questions.question: Which element is intended for a table header cell?
questions.explanation: Th identifies a header cell and supports accessible table relationships.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Th identifies a header cell and supports accessible table relationships.

questions.question: Which element provides a table caption?
questions.explanation: Caption gives a table its title or description.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Caption gives a table its title or description.

questions.question: What is the purpose of colspan on a table cell?
questions.explanation: Colspan makes a cell span multiple columns.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Colspan makes a cell span multiple columns.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rowspan?
options: Make a cell span multiple rows
questions.explanation: Rowspan makes a cell occupy multiple rows.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Rowspan makes a cell occupy multiple rows.

questions.question: Why should tables generally not be used for page layout?
options: They are meant for tabular data and can make layout less flexible and accessible
questions.explanation: Use CSS layout tools for page layout and tables for genuinely tabular data.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Use CSS layout tools for page layout and tables for genuinely tabular data.

questions.question: Which element is intended for the main unique content of a page?
questions.explanation: Main identifies the dominant content; normally there should not be multiple visible main elements.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Main identifies the dominant content; normally there should not be multiple visible main elements.

questions.question: Which element groups major navigation links?
questions.explanation: Nav identifies a navigation section.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Nav identifies a navigation section.

questions.question: Which element is appropriate for a self-contained blog post?
questions.explanation: Article is intended for independently reusable or distributable content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Article is intended for independently reusable or distributable content.

questions.question: Which element groups thematically related content, often with a heading?
questions.explanation: Section groups related content; use a heading when appropriate.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Section groups related content; use a heading when appropriate.

questions.question: Which element is suitable for tangentially related content?
questions.explanation: Aside is commonly used for sidebars or related supplementary content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Aside is commonly used for sidebars or related supplementary content.

questions.question: Which element commonly represents introductory or navigational content for a page or section?
questions.explanation: Header is visible structural content, unlike head which holds document metadata.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Header is visible structural content, unlike head which holds document metadata.

questions.question: Which element commonly contains closing information or footer links?
questions.explanation: Footer can contain author, copyright, or related links.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Footer can contain author, copyright, or related links.

questions.question: What is a benefit of semantic HTML?
options: It communicates structure and meaning to browsers and assistive technologies
questions.explanation: Semantics improve the machine-readable structure of a page.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Semantics improve the machine-readable structure of a page.

questions.question: Should every group of content be a section element?
options: No; use section for a meaningful thematic grouping
questions.explanation: Use generic containers when no semantic grouping is needed.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Use generic containers when no semantic grouping is needed.

questions.question: What is the difference between <head> and <header>?
options: Head holds document metadata; header is visible introductory content
Header holds metadata; head is visible
questions.explanation: The names are similar but their roles are very different.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The names are similar but their roles are very different.

questions.question: Which element creates a form?
questions.explanation: Form groups controls that can submit data.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Form groups controls that can submit data.

questions.question: Which attribute names a submitted form field?
questions.explanation: The name is typically used as the key in submitted form data.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The name is typically used as the key in submitted form data.

questions.question: What connects a label to a form control?
questions.explanation: Matching for and id improves usability and accessible naming.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Matching for and id improves usability and accessible naming.

questions.question: Which input type supports built-in email-format checking?
questions.explanation: Email input provides browser-level format validation, not proof that the address exists.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Email input provides browser-level format validation, not proof that the address exists.

questions.question: Which control allows multiple independent selections?
questions.explanation: Checkboxes allow zero, one, or several options to be selected.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Checkboxes allow zero, one, or several options to be selected.

questions.question: Which control is generally used when exactly one option should be chosen from a group?
options: Radio buttons sharing the same name
questions.explanation: Radio buttons with the same name form a single-choice group.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Radio buttons with the same name form a single-choice group.

questions.question: Which element creates a multi-line text input?
questions.explanation: Textarea accepts multiple lines of text.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Textarea accepts multiple lines of text.

questions.question: Which pair creates a native dropdown?
questions.explanation: Select contains option elements.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Select contains option elements.

questions.question: Which attribute makes a field mandatory in browser validation?
questions.explanation: Required activates built-in constraint validation for supported controls.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Required activates built-in constraint validation for supported controls.

questions.question: Which form method usually places submitted fields in the URL query string?
questions.explanation: GET is designed for retrieval and commonly places form parameters in the URL.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: GET is designed for retrieval and commonly places form parameters in the URL.

questions.question: Which encoding is required for a typical HTML form file upload?
questions.explanation: Multipart form data allows files and fields to be sent together.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Multipart form data allows files and fields to be sent together.

questions.question: What does a hidden input guarantee?
options: Only that the control is not displayed as a normal visible field
That users cannot change its value
questions.explanation: Hidden inputs can be inspected or changed; never trust them for security.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Hidden inputs can be inspected or changed; never trust them for security.

questions.question: What is the purpose of fieldset and legend?
options: Group related controls and label the group
questions.explanation: Fieldset groups related form controls; legend supplies the group caption.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Fieldset groups related form controls; legend supplies the group caption.

questions.question: What is the difference between disabled and readonly controls?
options: Disabled controls are generally not submitted; readonly controls can be submitted where supported
questions.explanation: Disabled controls are not focusable and usually omitted from submission; readonly values can still be submitted.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Disabled controls are not focusable and usually omitted from submission; readonly values can still be submitted.

questions.question: What does the button type='submit' do inside a form?
questions.explanation: A submit button initiates form submission and constraint validation unless overridden.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A submit button initiates form submission and constraint validation unless overridden.

questions.question: What does meta charset='UTF-8' declare?
questions.explanation: UTF-8 supports a broad range of characters and symbols.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: UTF-8 supports a broad range of characters and symbols.

questions.question: What does the viewport meta tag help with?
options: Mobile viewport sizing and responsive layout
questions.explanation: It helps mobile browsers use the device viewport width for responsive layouts.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: It helps mobile browsers use the device viewport width for responsive layouts.

questions.question: Where should a link to an external CSS stylesheet normally go?
questions.explanation: A link element with rel stylesheet is normally placed in head.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A link element with rel stylesheet is normally placed in head.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a meta description?
options: It guarantees a higher search ranking
It provides a page summary that search engines may use as a snippet
questions.explanation: Search engines may use it for snippets; it does not guarantee ranking or snippet display.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Search engines may use it for snippets; it does not guarantee ranking or snippet display.

questions.question: What does the lang attribute help with?
options: Pronunciation and language interpretation by assistive technologies and other tools
questions.explanation: Correct language metadata helps pronunciation and processing.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Correct language metadata helps pronunciation and processing.

questions.question: What is a canonical link used for?
options: Choosing a primary URL for substantially duplicate or similar content
questions.explanation: Canonical hints help search engines understand the preferred URL.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Canonical hints help search engines understand the preferred URL.

questions.question: Which element sets the document title?
questions.explanation: Title is the document title; an h1 is visible page content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Title is the document title; an h1 is visible page content.

questions.question: Does adding semantic HTML guarantee high SEO rankings?
options: No; it helps structure and understanding but does not guarantee rankings
questions.explanation: SEO depends on many factors; no single element guarantees rankings.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: SEO depends on many factors; no single element guarantees rankings.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rel='stylesheet' on a link element?
questions.explanation: Rel tells the browser the linked resource is a stylesheet.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Rel tells the browser the linked resource is a stylesheet.

questions.question: What does the base element do?
options: Sets a base URL and/or default target for relative URLs
questions.explanation: Base in head changes how relative URLs are resolved, so use it carefully.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Base in head changes how relative URLs are resolved, so use it carefully.

questions.question: What should alt text do for an informative image?
options: Convey the relevant information or function of the image
questions.explanation: Good alt text depends on the image's purpose and context.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Good alt text depends on the image's purpose and context.

questions.question: How should a purely decorative image usually be marked?
questions.explanation: An empty alt allows assistive technology to ignore decorative imagery.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: An empty alt allows assistive technology to ignore decorative imagery.

questions.question: Why should form inputs have associated labels?
options: To provide an accessible name and enlarge the clickable label target
questions.explanation: Labels improve screen-reader support and usability.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Labels improve screen-reader support and usability.

questions.question: What is aria-label used for?
options: To provide an accessible name when appropriate
questions.explanation: Use ARIA only when native HTML does not already provide the needed accessible name.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Use ARIA only when native HTML does not already provide the needed accessible name.

questions.question: What should be preferred when a native HTML element provides the needed behavior?
options: A custom div with many ARIA attributes
questions.explanation: Native controls usually provide built-in keyboard, focus, and accessibility behavior.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Native controls usually provide built-in keyboard, focus, and accessibility behavior.

questions.question: What does tabindex='-1' generally do?
options: Allows programmatic focus but removes it from normal sequential Tab navigation
Makes it the first Tab stop
questions.explanation: It is often used for focus management, such as moving focus to a dialog heading.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: It is often used for focus management, such as moving focus to a dialog heading.

questions.question: Why is keyboard navigation important?
options: Only because search engines require it
Some users navigate without a mouse, and keyboard access is a core accessibility requirement
questions.explanation: Interactive controls should be operable with a keyboard.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Interactive controls should be operable with a keyboard.

questions.question: Which is the best button label for a button displaying only an X icon?
questions.explanation: A meaningful accessible name communicates the action.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A meaningful accessible name communicates the action.

questions.question: Should ARIA replace semantic HTML everywhere?
options: No; use native semantics first and ARIA when needed
questions.explanation: The first rule of ARIA is generally to use native HTML semantics where possible.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The first rule of ARIA is generally to use native HTML semantics where possible.

questions.question: Why should heading levels be used logically?
options: They communicate the content hierarchy and aid navigation
questions.explanation: Headings form an outline-like hierarchy for readers and assistive technology.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Headings form an outline-like hierarchy for readers and assistive technology.

questions.question: Which element embeds video?
questions.explanation: Video embeds video content and can contain source elements and fallback text.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Video embeds video content and can contain source elements and fallback text.

questions.question: Which element embeds audio?
questions.explanation: Audio embeds sound content.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Audio embeds sound content.

questions.question: Which attribute displays built-in playback controls?
questions.explanation: Controls requests browser-provided media controls.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Controls requests browser-provided media controls.

questions.question: Which element is used to embed another browsing context, often another page?
questions.explanation: Iframe embeds another browsing context; security and privacy settings matter.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Iframe embeds another browsing context; security and privacy settings matter.

questions.question: How does SVG differ from canvas?
options: SVG uses scalable vector graphics in the DOM; canvas is a pixel drawing surface
questions.explanation: SVG elements remain individually addressable; canvas drawing is primarily pixel-based.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: SVG elements remain individually addressable; canvas drawing is primarily pixel-based.

questions.question: Which technology is typically used to draw custom pixels with JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Canvas exposes a drawing surface controlled through scripting.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Canvas exposes a drawing surface controlled through scripting.

questions.question: What does the source element do inside picture or audio/video?
questions.explanation: Source lets the browser choose among supplied media resources.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Source lets the browser choose among supplied media resources.

questions.question: What is a key consideration when embedding third-party content with iframe?
options: Consider permissions, sandboxing, privacy, and trusted origins
It automatically inherits all page styles
questions.explanation: Iframe content can be isolated or restricted with appropriate attributes and policy.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Iframe content can be isolated or restricted with appropriate attributes and policy.

questions.question: What does defer do for an external classic script?
options: Downloads without blocking parsing and executes after parsing, preserving order among deferred scripts
Runs only if JavaScript is disabled
questions.explanation: Deferred classic scripts execute after parsing and in document order.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Deferred classic scripts execute after parsing and in document order.

questions.question: How does async differ from defer?
options: Async execution order is not guaranteed; it executes when downloaded
Async always waits for parsing to finish
questions.explanation: Async is useful for independent scripts; defer is useful when order matters.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Async is useful for independent scripts; defer is useful when order matters.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the noscript element?
options: Show fallback content when scripting is unavailable or disabled
questions.explanation: Noscript provides fallback content for browsers that do not execute scripts.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Noscript provides fallback content for browsers that do not execute scripts.

questions.question: What does contenteditable='true' do?
options: Automatically saves content to a server
Allows the element's content to be edited in the browser
questions.explanation: It enables editing but does not automatically persist changes.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: It enables editing but does not automatically persist changes.

questions.question: What is the template element used for?
options: Content rendered immediately in every case
Holding inert HTML that can be cloned and inserted later
questions.explanation: Template contents are not rendered as normal page content until used.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Template contents are not rendered as normal page content until used.

questions.question: What does dialog.showModal() do?
options: Opens a modal dialog with a backdrop and modal behavior
questions.explanation: ShowModal places the dialog in the top layer and makes the rest of the document modal.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: ShowModal places the dialog in the top layer and makes the rest of the document modal.

questions.question: What does data-user-id='42' map to in JavaScript dataset?
questions.explanation: Hyphenated data attribute names are exposed in camelCase through dataset.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Hyphenated data attribute names are exposed in camelCase through dataset.

questions.question: What is Shadow DOM commonly used for?
options: Encapsulating a component's internal markup and styles
questions.explanation: Shadow DOM helps isolate component internals from the surrounding document.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Shadow DOM helps isolate component internals from the surrounding document.

questions.question: What does localStorage do?
options: Stores data that generally persists until cleared
Stores data only on a server
Sends every value with each request automatically
questions.explanation: Local storage is client-side storage and is not automatically sent with HTTP requests.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Local storage is client-side storage and is not automatically sent with HTTP requests.

questions.question: Does putting a secret in a hidden input make it secure?
options: No, users can inspect or alter it
Yes, if its name starts with underscore
questions.explanation: Hidden fields are client-controlled input and must not be trusted as secret or authoritative.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Hidden fields are client-controlled input and must not be trusted as secret or authoritative.

questions.question: Can HTML client-side validation be bypassed?
options: Yes; server-side validation is also needed
questions.explanation: Client-side checks improve usability but are not a security boundary.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Client-side checks improve usability but are not a security boundary.

questions.question: What happens if an input has required but is empty during normal form submission?
options: The browser typically blocks submission and reports a validation error
The browser fills a random value
questions.explanation: Built-in constraint validation prevents ordinary submission until the field is valid.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Built-in constraint validation prevents ordinary submission until the field is valid.

questions.question: Which is the best approach to spacing and colors?
options: Use table cells for every gap
questions.explanation: Separate structure from presentation for maintainability.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Separate structure from presentation for maintainability.

questions.question: Should an id be repeated across many unrelated elements on the same page?
options: No; IDs should be unique within the document
questions.explanation: Duplicate IDs can cause incorrect label, script, and fragment behavior.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Duplicate IDs can cause incorrect label, script, and fragment behavior.

questions.question: What is a common risk of using target='_blank' without appropriate link handling?
options: The opened page may gain access to the opener in some contexts
questions.explanation: Using rel=noopener is a safe, common practice for new browsing contexts.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Using rel=noopener is a safe, common practice for new browsing contexts.

questions.question: Does an HTML comment hide sensitive information from users?
questions.explanation: Comments are included in the document source and must not contain secrets.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Comments are included in the document source and must not contain secrets.

questions.question: What is the role of the action attribute on a form?
options: It specifies the submission destination URL
questions.explanation: Action tells the browser where to send form data.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Action tells the browser where to send form data.

questions.question: What is progressive enhancement?
options: Build only for the newest browser
Start with robust core content and add enhancements where supported
questions.explanation: Core content and functionality should remain available as enhancements are added.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Core content and functionality should remain available as enhancements are added.

questions.question:
What text appears as the top-level heading?

Welcome
questions.explanation: The browser renders Welcome as a level-one heading.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The browser renders Welcome as a level-one heading.

questions.question: What does About do?
options: Creates a link to a relative path named about.html
questions.explanation: The anchor's href points to a relative URL.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The anchor's href points to a relative URL.

questions.question: What is the value of document.getElementById('u').dataset.userId when the element has data-user-id='42'?
questions.explanation: Dataset values are strings; the camelCase property is userId.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Dataset values are strings; the camelCase property is userId.

questions.question: What is wrong with from an accessibility perspective if the image is informative?
options: Images cannot be used in HTML
It lacks an appropriate text alternative
questions.explanation: Informative images should normally have meaningful alt text.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Informative images should normally have meaningful alt text.

questions.question: What happens when a button inside a form has no type attribute in ordinary HTML form usage?
options: It is always a reset button
It generally behaves as a submit button
questions.explanation: A button associated with a form defaults to submit behavior unless otherwise specified.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A button associated with a form defaults to submit behavior unless otherwise specified.

questions.question: What does <input type='checkbox' checked> mean?
questions.explanation: Checked sets the initial checked state in markup.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Checked sets the initial checked state in markup.

questions.question:
Which is the proper way to show literal

in visible text?
questions.explanation: Escape the angle brackets so the browser treats them as text.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Escape the angle brackets so the browser treats them as text.

questions.question: What is the likely purpose of <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>?
questions.explanation: It helps establish the viewport dimensions and initial scale.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: It helps establish the viewport dimensions and initial scale.

questions.question: CSS stands for?
questions.explanation: CSS controls the presentation of HTML.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: CSS controls the presentation of HTML.

questions.question: Which HTML element contains internal CSS?
questions.explanation: Use the style element, commonly inside head.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Use the style element, commonly inside head.

questions.question: Which element links an external stylesheet?
questions.explanation: Use <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: Use <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">.

questions.question: Which attribute applies inline CSS?
questions.explanation: The style attribute contains declarations for that element.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: The style attribute contains declarations for that element.

questions.question: Correct CSS syntax?
questions.explanation: A rule has a selector and declaration block.
questions.simpleExplanation: Remember: A rule has a selector and declaration block.

questions.question: CSS comments use?
questions.explanation: CSS comments start with /* and end with */.
